name: ECC
description: The agent harness performance optimization system. Skills, instincts, memory, security, and research-first development for Claude Code, Codex, Opencode, Cursor and beyond.
one_liner: A plugin that makes AI coding assistants remember past work, follow safety rules, and work faster across several different AI coding tools.
buyer: A CTO at a small software shop who already pays for Claude Code or Cursor seats and wants those tools to retain project context and enforce security checks without buying a separate enterprise platform.
business_use_cases: A dev shop installs it across every engineer's AI coding tool so security guardrails and memory persist the same way regardless of which tool (Cursor, Codex, Claude Code) a given developer prefers.
A consultant charges clients a setup fee to configure ECC's memory and skill system on client codebases so the client's own in-house AI assistant performs better after the engagement ends.
An open-source maintainer uses it to keep an AI agent's understanding of a large codebase consistent across many short contributor sessions.

money_ideas.idea: Charge for the GitHub App / private-repo tier for teams that want managed installs and support.
Offer paid onboarding to configure ECC's memory and security profile for a specific enterprise codebase.

steal_this: This weekend, write a short paid guide comparing ECC to similar agent-harness tools and sell it to teams evaluating which one to standardize on.
